newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes renew attacks on Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes renew attacks on Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli planes attacked Hizbollah targets in south Lebanon again on Friday evening -- their third raid on the area since guerrillas killed three Israeli soldiers, Lebanese security sources said.
They said two warplanes fired four rockets into the hills of Daidaba in the area of Jabal ad-Dahr south of the Syrian-controlled Bekaa Valley.
The sources said the air raids were followed by artillery shelling of the area. There was no immediate word on casualties.
The attack, which brought to 33 the total number of Israeli air attacks into Lebanon this year, came after Israel said that it had no territorial designs on Lebanon and wanted to talk peace.

"Israel has already clarified several times that it has no territorial interest in Lebanon. We are interested in reaching a real agreement in Lebanon," Israel's Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said earlier on the day in Israel.

Hizbollah guerrillas killed three Israeli soldiers and wounded seven overnight in fierce clashes just outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. The guerrillas said they ambushed the soldiers as they attempted to infiltrate outside the zone.
The deaths brought to nine the number of Israeli soldiers killed and to 35 the number of wounded in guerrilla attacks in south Lebanon in 1997.
Shortly after the clashes, Israeli helicptors struck into the area. They hit again on Friday morning.
A Lebanese Army spokesman said that during Thursday night's clash an Israeli helicopter fired a rocket at a Lebanese army position, destroying an armoured vehicle but causing no casualties.
Israel's northern army commander, Amiram Levine, in a news conference broadcast on Israel Radio, said there was an exchange of fire between Israeli and Lebanese forces.
"Usually the Lebanese Army is not our enemy... but anyone who participates in battle with Hizbollah and obstructs Israeli army operations and endangers it will be hit," Levine said.
Hizbollah is fighting to oust the Israeli troops from the 15 km (nine miles)-wide strip they occupy in south Lebanon.
In Beirut, Hizbollah leader Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah said on Friday: "If Jews do not return to where they came from, the Islamic guerrillas' fists will throw all invaders and occupiers in the sea."
